# RV power station and solar combos

The best pick depends on whether you need to run a roof AC. The search results don't include panel pricing or direct buy links for most of these, so I've linked the pages I used.

## Top picks

**1. Best value for big power: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, 3,600 W continuous at 120 V (6,000 W peak), with an RV outlet.
- Solar input is up to 2,000 W across three 650 W inputs. You'd need panels on all three inputs to reach that.
- The store price is $1,499. With code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200) it's about $1,319.12, and the code expires 2026-11-15. Stores usually take one code per order, and checkout has the final word.
- It has a 5-year warranty and a 30-day return window, and sale items may not be returnable. At 45 kg (about 99 lb) it's heavy.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

**2. Best for full-time boondocking: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous and 8,000 W surge, expandable past 12 kWh.
- It recharges from 0 to 80% in about 50 minutes on wall power.
- It's the most expensive option once you add batteries, and it takes two people to lift.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**3. Best for running the AC on weekend trips: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- 3,024 Wh, 3,000 W continuous and 6,000 W surge. That's enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC, which draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**4. Best mid-range: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, a built-in 30A RV port and up to 1,200 W of solar input. It's about 62 lb.
- Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**5. Best for light use (fridge, Starlink, laptop, CPAP): EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, and up to 1,000 W of solar input through two 500 W inputs.
- It's about 28 lb and expandable to 5 kWh.
- Source: [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Solar panels
- **Match panels to the station's solar input limit.** Jackery's 1000 v2, for example, caps at 400 W, so extra panels won't charge it faster ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- A 300–400 W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- For smaller setups, [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife) suggests a Renogy 200W folding suitcase or a 100W foldable panel.
- A roof-mounted array on a big rig can use much more solar than a folding panel, but only if the station accepts it. The R4000, DELTA Pro 3 and AC200L have the highest ceilings.

## My recommendation
- **Running the AC or full-timing:** the ALLPOWERS R4000 is the cheapest per kWh here, but it's the least established brand. The DELTA Pro 3 is the premium choice.
- **Weekend trips without AC:** the DELTA 3 Plus or Jackery 1000 v2, plus 200–400 W of folding panels.

Some reviews disagree on specs and are older, such as the AC200P figures in one comparison, so check current specs on the retailer's page before buying.

What size is your RV, and do you need to run the roof AC? Knowing that would let me narrow this to one pick.
